definition: Unpaid principal balance: what the borrower still owes.
why: Pricing, pool sizes and weighted averages all use current UPB.

definition: Weighted-average coupon: note rates averaged by current UPB.
why: Sets which agency coupons a pool can fit.

definition: An average where each loan counts in proportion to its current UPB: sum(value x UPB) / sum(UPB). WA FICO and WA LTV are the pool's FICO and LTV weighted this way.
why: A $900,000 loan moves a pool's value ten times more than a $90,000 one, so desks and investors quote pools by weighted, not simple, averages.

definition: Weighted-average loan age, in months.
why: Seasoning changes prepayment and credit behavior.

definition: Borrower credit score, from 300 to 850.
why: The main credit signal; low-FICO loans price differently.

definition: Debt-to-income: monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income, in percent.
why: Measures ability to pay; high DTI raises default risk.

definition: Loan-to-value at origination, in percent: LTV = (loan amount / appraised property value) x 100.
why: The equity cushion; higher LTV means a bigger loss if the loan defaults.

definition: Combined LTV: the first lien plus drawn subordinate liens, divided by value.
why: Shows total leverage on the property.

definition: High combined LTV: CLTV using the full HELOC line, drawn or not.
why: Worst-case leverage if the borrower draws the whole line.

definition: Mark-to-market LTV: current UPB divided by today's estimated value.
why: Above 100, the borrower owes more than the home is worth.

definition: Days-past-due status by the Mortgage Bankers Association method: Current, 30, 60, 90, 120+, foreclosure, bankruptcy, REO.
why: The industry-standard way to measure credit performance.

definition: Real estate owned: the lender owns the property after foreclosure.
why: The loan is now a property to sell, usually at a loss.

definition: Low loan balance: spec-pool tiers by maximum original balance. LoanIQ's tiers are listed in backend/app/config/spec_stories.toml.
why: Small loans tend to prepay more slowly, so investors pay more for them.

definition: To-be-announced: forward trading of agency MBS by program, term, coupon and settlement month.
why: The benchmark price for agency loans and the main hedge for a pipeline.

definition: A pool of loans that share a story, such as low balance, high LTV or New York, and trade above TBA.
why: The pay-up over TBA is extra execution value.

definition: A file with one row per loan: program, balance, rate, borrower, property and payment status.
why: It is what a seller sends the desk, and every pricing and pooling decision starts from it.

definition: Government-sponsored enterprise: the companies chartered by Congress that buy conforming loans from lenders and guarantee agency MBS (UMBS).
why: They are the main buyers of conventional loans, so their rules decide which loans are agency-eligible.

definition: The largest loan the GSEs can buy, set each year by FHFA; high-cost areas allow up to 150% of the baseline.
why: It separates agency loans from Jumbo loans, which sell to different buyers at different prices.

definition: A loan with no government insurance, at or under the conforming limit, sold to the GSEs.
why: The largest program; it delivers into agency UMBS pools.

definition: The loan feature that puts a loan in a spec pool, such as low balance, New York, Puerto Rico or low FICO. LoanIQ's stories and their rules are in backend/app/config/spec_stories.toml.
why: Each story earns a different pay-up over TBA, so tagging loans by story is the first step of best execution.

definition: A conforming loan above the baseline limit but under the high-cost-area ceiling.
why: Agencies buy it, but it has its own pool rules and usually a worse price than a standard conforming loan.

definition: A loan above the conforming limit, so the agencies cannot buy it.
why: It sells to banks or into private-label securities, priced on credit rather than to TBA.

definition: A loan insured by the Federal Housing Administration, allowing low down payments and lower credit scores.
why: It goes into Ginnie Mae pools; the government insurance offsets weaker borrower credit.

definition: A loan guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs for veterans and service members, up to 100% LTV.
why: It goes into Ginnie Mae pools; no down payment, but the guarantee protects the investor.

definition: A rural-housing loan guaranteed by the US Department of Agriculture, up to 100% LTV.
why: It goes into Ginnie Mae pools; a small program with its own eligibility.

definition: A loan outside the Qualified Mortgage rules, such as interest-only, bank-statement income or high DTI.
why: It cannot go into agency pools, so it carries higher rates and sells to private investors.

definition: The interest rate on the borrower's mortgage note, in percent.
why: It sets which security coupons the loan can go into and how much servicing it can pay.

definition: The monthly principal and interest payment on the amortization schedule.
why: Taxes and insurance excluded, it is what the borrower must pay, and what passes through to investors.

definition: Paying a loan down over its term with level monthly payments that are mostly interest early on and mostly principal later.
why: It drives current UPB, and so pool balances and cash flows.

definition: The number of monthly payments that have come due since the first payment date.
why: Seasoned loans prepay and default differently from new ones.

definition: Adjustable-rate mortgage. A 5/6 ARM is fixed for 5 years, then resets every 6 months to index plus margin.
why: Resets can cause payment shock and prepayment, so ARMs price and pool separately from fixed-rate loans.

definition: Secured Overnight Financing Rate, the US benchmark that replaced LIBOR; ARMs use its 30-day average.
why: It is the index ARM rates reset to.

definition: The fixed spread, in percent, added to the index when an ARM resets.
why: Index plus margin is the borrower's new rate, subject to caps.

definition: Limits on ARM rate changes, written initial/periodic/lifetime in percentage points, e.g. 2/1/5.
why: They bound payment shock and the investor's upside.

definition: A loan where the payment covers only interest for a set period, so the balance does not fall.
why: More leverage for longer; a Non-QM feature that raises credit risk.

definition: The lender that originated the loan and is selling it to the desk.
why: Seller quality and reps and warranties affect what the desk will pay.

definition: The company that collects payments and handles delinquencies for the loan's owner.
why: Servicing is valuable and is priced separately from the loan.

definition: How the loan was sourced: Retail (the lender's own), Correspondent (bought closed from another lender) or Broker.
why: Channel affects loan quality and the cost of acquiring the loan.

definition: How the borrower uses the property: primary residence, second home or investment property.
why: Investors default more often, so they carry higher rates and lower LTV limits.

definition: A refinance in which the borrower borrows more than they owe and takes the difference in cash.
why: It adds leverage and is riskier than a rate/term refinance, so it has lower LTV limits.

definition: A borrower who has not owned a home recently and is buying one to live in.
why: A common affordability and spec-pool story; these borrowers have less equity.

definition: Home equity line of credit: a second lien the borrower can draw on up to a limit.
why: An undrawn line can become debt at any time, which is why HCLTV counts the full line.

definition: House Price Index: how much home values changed over time, such as FHFA's index.
why: It moves appraised value to today's value, which gives mark-to-market LTV.

definition: Home Affordable Refinance Program: an FHFA program (ended 2018) that let underwater borrowers refinance above 125% LTV.
why: The source of agency loans with original LTV above 125, which form their own pools.

definition: Calendar days since the oldest unpaid payment was due.
why: It places a loan in its MBA delinquency bucket.

definition: A 12-character string showing each month's payment status, oldest first.
why: Buyers look for clean recent history; a single past 30-day late can make a loan ineligible.

definition: A permanent change to a loan's terms, such as rate or term, to help a struggling borrower.
why: Modified loans are riskier and have their own pricing and pool rules.

definition: A temporary pause or reduction of payments agreed with the servicer.
why: Loans in or just out of forbearance usually cannot be pooled until they reperform.

definition: A loan 90 or more days past due or in foreclosure, by the MBA method. LoanIQ's "90+ / FC / REO / BK" desk question also counts bankrupt and REO loans.
why: These loans cannot go into an agency pool and are priced as distressed assets, far below TBA.

definition: A one-click question a trader asks of every new tape, such as LTV over 125 or New York. Each shows how many loans answer it and filters the grid to them. LoanIQ's questions and their rules are in backend/app/config/desk_questions.toml.
why: It finds the loans that change the price or cannot be pooled, before anyone quotes a bid.

definition: The starting number for the random generator; the same seed rebuilds the same synthetic tape.
why: Every demo and test sees the same loans.

definition: One step of the Ask the Tape agent: the AI model asks LoanIQ to run a named tool (query_tape, summarize_tape, lookup_term, list_columns or get_loan), and LoanIQ's code runs it and returns the result. The model never touches the data itself.
why: Every number in an answer comes from a tool result, and the screen shows each call with its SQL, so a trader can check the answer instead of trusting it.

definition: A check LoanIQ runs on every tool call before it touches the tape: one read-only SELECT, the loans table only, known columns, values bound as parameters, a row cap and a time limit. A refused call goes back to the model with the reason.
why: An AI model writes the SQL, so the code, not the model, decides what may run. Nothing the model writes can change the tape or read anything else.

definition: An Ask the Tape answer's SQL, kept in your browser (the last 5) under a short tag, so one click reruns it on the tape without asking the model again.
why: The desk asks the same questions of every tape. A saved query answers in milliseconds, at no AI cost, with exactly the same rule each time.

definition: LoanIQ's own answers, with no AI model: the desk questions (LTV over 125, New York and the others) and a tape summary, computed by the same tools. Ask the Tape switches to them when the server has no AI key, when a daily limit is reached, or when the model fails.
why: The screen always answers, says plainly that the model did not, and never spends past its budget.

definition: An AI model that answers by planning each step and calling LoanIQ's own tools, not from memory.
why: The tools do every calculation on the tape and show their SQL, so the desk can check each answer; the model only plans and explains.

definition: Deciding, for every loan on the tape, which agency pool it can go into (UMBS or GNMA II), at which pass-through coupons, and which spec stories it fits. Loans that fail a check are not slotted, with the reason. LoanIQ's rules are in backend/app/config/slotting.toml.
why: A tape can only be priced once it is slotted: Best Execution prices each slot and picks the highest.

definition: Where one loan can go: its agency, term and coupons, written like UMBS 30Y 2.5 / 3.0.
why: It tells the desk at a glance which TBA price grid applies to the loan.

definition: Uniform mortgage-backed security: the single TBA security Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac both issue for conforming conventional loans, High-Balance included.
why: The main agency pool for conventional loans, and the most traded TBA market.

definition: Ginnie Mae II: pools of government-insured loans (FHA, VA, USDA), guaranteed by the US government.
why: The agency pool for government loans; it is priced off its own TBA grid.

definition: The interest rate a pool pays its investors, in percent: the loans' note rate minus the strip. Agency TBA coupons trade in half-point steps (2.5, 3.0, 3.5).
why: TBA prices are quoted by coupon, so a loan's coupon decides which price it gets.

definition: The part of the note rate that does not reach investors: the servicer's fee plus the agency's guarantee fee. LoanIQ uses one illustrative minimum strip, set in slotting.toml.
why: The strip decides the highest coupon a loan can support; a bigger strip means a lower coupon.

definition: The two coupons LoanIQ gives each slotted loan: the down coupon is the note rate minus the minimum strip, rounded down to the coupon step; the up coupon is one step higher.
why: The seller can deliver at either; Best Execution prices both and keeps the better one.

definition: A slotted loan with no spec story. It goes into an ordinary TBA pool at its coupon, with no pay-up.
why: It is the price every slotted loan can always get; a spec story is worth something only if it beats it.

definition: A loan no agency pool will take under LoanIQ's rules: its program has no agency pool (Jumbo, Non-QM), its product has no TBA coupon (ARMs), or it is not current.
why: These loans need another execution, such as a whole-loan sale, and are priced separately.

definition: The pass-through coupon that would trade at par (100) today. LoanIQ takes Treasury's par yield at each product's anchor tenor and adds an illustrative spread (backend/app/config/pricing.toml).
why: Coupons above it trade at a premium and coupons below it at a discount; pay-ups and prepayment speeds key off each coupon's gap to it.

definition: A price of 100: the bond trades at its face value.
why: The dividing line between discount and premium coupons, and the price prepaid principal comes back at.

definition: How TBA prices are quoted: points and 32nds of a point, with + for half a 32nd. 98-08+ is 98 + 8.5/32 = 98.265625; a pay-up of 18+ is 18.5/32 of a point.
why: Every dealer and trader quotes this way, so the screen speaks the desk's language.

definition: What a spec pool is worth over the TBA price at the same coupon, in 32nds. LoanIQ's sizes are illustrative (backend/app/config/spec_stories.toml) and grow from nothing on discount coupons to the full size on premium ones.
why: Best execution adds it to the TBA price when a loan fits a spec story.

definition: A coupon outside the product's traded band: LoanIQ's model prices it, but no one would trade it today. The bands are in backend/app/config/pricing.toml.
why: It keeps the grid complete without pretending a deep-discount or deep-premium coupon has a market.

definition: The next TBA delivery month whose 48-hour notification date has not passed, for the product's SIFMA class. It rolls to the following month the day after that date.
why: A TBA trade settles in a named month; Current is the one most trades are quoted for.

definition: SIFMA's groups of products that share settlement dates: Class A is 30-year UMBS, B is 15-year UMBS and Ginnie Mae, C is 30-year Ginnie Mae. LoanIQ's product-to-class map is in backend/app/config/pricing.toml.
why: Products in different classes roll to the next month on different days.

definition: The 48-hour day before settlement, when sellers tell buyers which pools they will deliver. SIFMA publishes it for each class and month.
why: Current rolls to the next month the day after it.

definition: The day TBA pools are delivered and paid for, set by SIFMA for each class and month.
why: The days between two settlement dates set the drop's financing cost.

definition: The Current price minus the next month's, shown in 32nds: one month of coupon, less the cost of financing the bonds until next month's settlement, plus principal prepaid at par.
why: It tells a seller whether to deliver now or roll to next month. A negative drop means next month trades higher.

definition: Conditional prepayment rate: the share of a pool's balance prepaid in a year, in percent. LoanIQ's illustrative range for the drop, from discounts to premiums, is in backend/app/config/pricing.toml [drop].
why: Prepaid principal comes back at par: a gain on a discount coupon, a loss on a premium one.

definition: Single monthly mortality: CPR as a monthly rate. SMM = 1 − (1 − CPR)^(1/12), so 12% CPR is about 1.06% a month.
why: The drop works one month at a time, so it needs the monthly rate.

definition: The cost of borrowing to hold the bonds until next month's settlement, in percent a year (actual/360): the 1-month Treasury bill yield plus an illustrative spread (backend/app/config/pricing.toml [drop]).
why: When financing costs more than the coupon earns, the drop turns negative.
